summary: Erich Haenisch studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (Ph.D. 1899–1904) under Wilhelm Grube, Richard Pischel, and Jules Oppert. Working in Sinology and Tibetology, he held professorships at Berlin, Leipzig (1925–1931), and Munich (1927–1951).

Erich Heintel was an Austrian philosopher who earned his doctorate (~1931–1936) and Habilitation (1940) at the University of Vienna. He served there as professor of philosophy from 1952 to 1982 and became a member of the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Erich Herold was a Czech Indologist who studied at Charles University under Oldřich Friš and Vincenc Lesný, earning his Ph.D. in 1947. He later served as director of the Náprstek Museum from 1959 to 1970.

Philosopher Erich Rudolf Jaensch studied at Breslau, Göttingen (Ph.D. ~1904–1908), and Strasbourg. He held professorships at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (1912–1913) and the University of Marburg, where he was appointed in 1913.
Erich Wolff was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg and completed his Ph.D. at Heidelberg University (1924–1930) under the supervision of Max Walleser.

Erich von Voss, who worked in Indology and linguistics, studied at the University of Tartu and earned his Ph.D. at the University of Leipzig (~1903–1906). He taught German and Greek at Petrischule from circa 1906 to 1917.

Erik Braun is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his doctorate at Harvard University under Janet Gyatso, also studying with Jonathan Evans, John Okell, and Saw Tun. He has held faculty positions at Harvard and the University of Virginia.

Erik Erikson studied at the University of Oxford. Over his career, he held positions at the University of California, Berkeley (~1939–1950), the University of Pittsburgh (~1951–1960), and Harvard University (~1960–1970).

Erik Gren studied classical history and archaeology at Uppsala University from circa 1923 to 1941. He worked as an assistant librarian at Uppsala University Library from 1931 and became Privatdozent of classical history at Uppsala in 1941.

Erik Haarh studied at Copenhagen under teachers including Kaare Grønbech and Poul Tuxen, earning his Ph.D. He worked at the Royal Danish Library and Copenhagen before serving as professor of history of religions at Aarhus University (1983–1987).

Erik J. Hammerstrom, a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology, earned his Ph.D. from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010). He served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).

Linguist Erik Johan Tammelin studied at Helsinki (Ph.D. ~1886–1890) and Jena under Berthold Delbrück. He served at the National Board of Education as chief inspector of classical languages (1894) and head of its secondary schools department (1918).
Erik Pema Kunsang works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Around 1981, he became director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications and a resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

Erik Zürcher studied at Leiden University (Ph.D. ~1947–1959) and under Paul Demiéville. A specialist in Sinology and Buddhist studies, he served as a director at Leiden University (1961–1993) and co-edited T'oung Pao (1975–1992).

Erik-Jan Zürcher earned his BA and PhD at Leiden University. Specializing in history and linguistics, he held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen, the International Institute of Social History (director 2008–2012), and became professor of Turkish language and culture at Leiden in 1997.

Erika Forte works in history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She was a research associate at Ruhr University Bochum (2018–2019) and a professor at the Italian School of East Asian Studies (attested 2026).
Erika Sandman works in linguistics, Sinology, and Tibetology. She completed her Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Helsinki (2007–2016) and later held a post there.
Erling von Mende studied Sinology at Bonn and earned his PhD and Habilitation at Cologne. He served as professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin from 1983 to 2007.

Ermenegildo La Terza studied at the University of Naples Federico II under Michele Kerbaker. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he taught at Messina (1923–1924) and held posts teaching Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Naples (1904; 1925–1935).
Ernest Arthur Gardner was a scholar of history and archaeology. He studied at Gonville and Caius College from circa 1880 to 1884 and later held a post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.
